nodes.summary: Let $R_9(m)$ denote the number of partitions of $m$ in which no part is divisible by $9$. For every positive integer $n$, $R_9(4n + 1) \equiv R_9(n) \pmod 3$.
nodes.title: A congruence for 9-regular partitions at $4n + 1$

nodes.summary: Let $R_9(m)$ denote the number of partitions of $m$ in which no part is divisible by $9$, and let $N_s = (4^s - 1)/3$. For all positive integers $r$ and $s$, $R_9((r - 1) 4^{s-1} + N_s) \equiv R_9(r) \pmod 3$, $R_9(N_s) \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, $R_9(4^{s-1} + N_s) \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ and $R_9(2 \cdot 4^{s-1} + N_s) \equiv 0 \pmod 3$.
nodes.title: Iterated congruences for 9-regular partitions modulo 3

nodes.summary: Let $R_9(m)$ denote the number of partitions of $m$ in which no part is divisible by $9$, and let $\sigma(m)$ be the sum of the positive divisors of $m$. For every positive integer $n$, $R_9(n) \equiv \sigma(3n + 1) \pmod 3$.
nodes.title: 9-regular partitions modulo 3 and the divisor sum

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $n$ a natural number. Let $R_p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part is divisible by $p$, and let $\tau_k(m)$ be the generalized tau function, the coefficient of $q^m$ in $q \prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - q^j)^k$. Then $R_p(n) \equiv \tau_{p-1}(n + 1) \pmod p$.
nodes.title: Prime-regular partitions and the generalized tau function

nodes.summary: Let $R_{25}(m)$ denote the number of partitions of $m$ in which no part is divisible by $25$, and let $\sigma(m)$ be the sum of the positive divisors of $m$. For every positive integer $n$, $R_{25}(n) \equiv (n + 1) \, \sigma(n + 1) \pmod 5$.
nodes.title: 25-regular partitions modulo 5 and the divisor sum

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a positive integer and $n$ a natural number. Let $R_{2^s}(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part is divisible by $2^s$, and let $\tau_k(m)$ be the generalized tau function, the coefficient of $q^m$ in $q \prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - q^j)^k$. Then $R_{2^s}(n) \equiv \tau_{2^s - 1}(n + 1) \pmod 2$.
nodes.title: $2^s$-regular partitions and the generalized tau function modulo 2

nodes.summary: Let $l$ be an odd prime, $k$ an integer with $1 \le k < l$, $n$ a natural number, and $r$ the remainder of $n$ modulo $l$. If $r \le l - k - 1$, then $\binom{n+k}{k} \equiv (-1)^r \binom{l-k-1}{r} \pmod l$; otherwise $\binom{n+k}{k} \equiv 0 \pmod l$.
nodes.title: Binomial coefficients $\binom{n+k}{k}$ modulo an odd prime

nodes.summary: The constant coefficient of the integer power series $\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - X^m)$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[X]]$ is $1$.
nodes.title: Euler's product has constant term $1$

nodes.summary: Let $\tau_k(m)$ be the generalized tau function, the coefficient of $q^m$ in $q \prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - q^j)^k$, and let $R_8(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ in which no part is divisible by $8$. For every positive integer $n$: (a) $\tau_{14}(2n + 1) \equiv R_8(n) \pmod 2$; (b) $\tau_6(2n + 1)$ is odd if and only if $n$ is a triangular number, that is, $n = m(m + 1)/2$ for some natural number $m$.
nodes.title: Parity of $\tau_{14}$ and $\tau_6$ at odd arguments

nodes.summary: Let $\tau_k(n)$ be the generalized tau function, the coefficient of $q^n$ in $q \prod_{j \ge 1} (1 - q^j)^k$. Let $k$ be an integer with $|k| \ge 2$ and $d$ a natural number dividing $|k|$ with $d < |k|$. Then for all natural numbers $m$ and $r$ with $\gcd(r, |k|/d) = 1$, $\tau_k(|k| m + d r + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{|k|/d}$.
nodes.title: Vanishing of the generalized tau function modulo $|k|/d$

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $k$ be a natural number such that $k - 1$ is prime. For an integer $t$ let $P(t) = t(3t - 1)/2$ be the generalized pentagonal number. If $k - 1$ does not divide $n - 1 - P(t)$ for any integer $t$ with $P(t) \le n - 1$, then the generalized tau function satisfies $\tau_k(n) \equiv 0 \pmod{k - 1}$.
nodes.title: Vanishing of $\tau_k(n)$ modulo the prime $k - 1$

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, $\tau_k(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series $q \bigl(\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)\bigr)^k$.

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $s \ge 1$ and $n \ge 0$ be natural numbers, and for an integer $t$ let $P(t) = t(3t - 1)/2$ be the generalized pentagonal number. Then $\tau_{p^s}(n + 1)$ is congruent modulo $p$ to the sum of $(-1)^t$ over the integers $t$ with $-n \le t \le n$ and $n = p^s P(t)$.

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $n$ a natural number, and for an integer $j$ let $P(j) = j(3j - 1)/2$ be the generalized pentagonal number. Then $\tau_{p^2 + 1}(n + 1)$ is congruent modulo $p$ to the sum of $(-1)^{r + s}$ over the pairs of integers $(r, s)$ with $-n \le r, s \le n$ and $n = P(r) + p^2 P(s)$.

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $n$ a natural number, and for an integer $j$ let $P(j) = j(3j - 1)/2$ be the generalized pentagonal number. nodes.summary: For an integer $k$ and a natural number $n$, the generalized tau function $\tau_k(n)$ is the coefficient of $q^n$ in the integer power series $q \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)^k$. For negative $k$ the power is taken in the group of units of $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$, where $\prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^m)$ is invertible because its constant term is $1$.
